You are checking whether this repository's documentation has fallen behind a pull request's
code changes.

Run `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (the base branch is `main`) to see what this PR actually
changed under `crates/**`. Compare that against `README.md` and everything under `docs/`
**except** `docs/reference/**` — that directory (the CLI reference, man pages, shell
completions, and the config/OpenAPI JSON Schemas) is mechanically regenerated by
`cargo run --locked -p bhtune-cli --example gen_docs --features schemars` and
`cargo run --locked -p bhtune-server --example gen_openapi`; it is already guaranteed fresh
by a `git diff --exit-code` gate in CI. Treat `docs/reference/**` as read-only ground truth for
the CLI's and config's current shape — read it to check narrative prose against, but never edit.

Update documentation only when the code diff changed something user-visible: a new or removed
CLI flag/subcommand, a config key, an HTTP endpoint, a changed default value, a template/catalog
field, or a safety rule. Do not rewrite unrelated sections, do not "improve" prose the diff
didn't touch, and do not add speculative or planned content.

Write documentation as state-of-the-world facts, not a changelog. "The CLI rejects
`--cycles-count 0`" is documentation; "Added validation for `--cycles-count`" is commit-message
language and does not belong in a file a reader opens to learn how the software behaves today.

Hard rules:

- Only edit files under `docs/` (excluding `docs/reference/**`) and `README.md`. Do not touch
  any other file — no source code, tests, workflows, or other config.
- Never edit `AGENTS.md`. If you believe something in it is now stale or should change, say so
  in your final response instead of editing the file — a human reviews that response and
  decides whether to act on it.
- If nothing documentation-worthy changed, say so plainly and make no edits at all. Making no
  changes is a perfectly good outcome and is expected for most PRs.
- Keep your final response short — a one- or two-line summary of what you changed, or why you
  changed nothing, is enough. It is posted as a PR comment verbatim.
